title: Couples — communication (session 3)

segments.speaker: therapist
segments.text: Welcome back, both of you. Since last time, what's been even a little bit better between you?

segments.speaker: client
segments.text: Honestly, not much. We had a big argument on Thursday about money again.

segments.speaker: client_2
segments.text: Although Tuesday was good. We cooked together, that was nice.

segments.speaker: therapist
segments.text: Tuesday was good. Tell me more about Tuesday. What was different?

segments.speaker: client_2
segments.text: We both got home early. Nobody was on their phone. We just talked while cooking.

segments.speaker: client
segments.text: Yeah, Tuesday was fine. I'd forgotten about Tuesday.

segments.speaker: therapist
segments.text: What did each of you do on Tuesday that helped it go well?

segments.speaker: client
segments.text: I suppose I asked about her day and actually listened.

segments.speaker: client_2
segments.text: And I didn't bring up the bills. I wanted to, but I didn't.

segments.speaker: therapist
segments.text: So you listened, and you chose to leave the bills for another time. That sounds like effort from both of you.

segments.speaker: client
segments.text: It's just that the bills need talking about at some point.

segments.speaker: therapist
segments.text: Of course. If the money conversation went the way you'd want it to, what would you notice?

segments.speaker: client
segments.text: We'd sit down at a set time, not in the middle of something else. And she wouldn't sigh at me.

segments.speaker: client_2
segments.text: And he wouldn't get defensive and walk out.

segments.speaker: therapist
segments.text: So a set time, calm, both staying in the room. On a scale from one to ten, where ten is money talks going the way you both want, where are you now?

segments.speaker: client
segments.text: Three.

segments.speaker: client_2
segments.text: Maybe four. We did agree the budget in the end on Thursday.

segments.speaker: therapist
segments.text: What would one point higher look like?

segments.speaker: client_2
segments.text: Maybe a fifteen-minute money check on Sunday evenings. With tea.

segments.speaker: client
segments.text: I could do Sundays. As long as it's fifteen minutes and not two hours.

segments.speaker: therapist
segments.text: A fifteen-minute money check on Sunday with tea. I'm struck by how quickly you both found something you could agree on.

segments.speaker: client
segments.text: We're not always this reasonable.

segments.speaker: therapist
segments.text: Between now and next time, could you each notice the moments when things are working between you, so we can hear about them?

segments.speaker: client_2
segments.text: Yes, we can do that.

expected_note_facts: Couple reported argument about money on Thursday
Tuesday was a better day: cooked together, no phones, talked
Partner A listened; partner B chose not to raise bills
Scaling of money conversations: 3 and 4 out of 10
Agreed 15-minute money check-in on Sunday evenings
Task: each notice moments when things are working

strengths: Opened with a 'what's better' question and amplified the Tuesday exception
Built a preferred future for money conversations
Used scaling and 'one point higher' to reach a small concrete step
missed_openings: Partner A's 'I'd forgotten about Tuesday' could have been explored
The sighing/defensive pattern could be explored in terms of what each would like instead
try_next: Ask each partner what they noticed the other doing well

review: CLINICAL-REVIEW: synthetic role-play; drafts for the Clinical Lead.
